text:
Desk learned of the matter when the arrival monitor flagged a service disruption affecting a companion animal booking and the traveler came to the counter seeking immediate guidance. Incident Report: Companion Animal Delay and Escalation

I took the report at the desk and confirmed the booking details against the ledger. The traveler said the pet crate had been accepted without issue, but the service path was interrupted after check-in and the animal had to remain in holding while staff sorted the transfer. The pet was calm on arrival, though the delay caused concern for the handler and required a review of welfare handling before any onward movement. I noted the account in plain terms and advised the traveler that the matter would be handled under standard desk procedure.

I then spoke with the senior coordinator, who reviewed the case and directed that the welfare coordinator inspect the animal area and confirm that the crate, water supply, and ventilation were acceptable. <<FACT F120>> The welfare coordinator confirmed the animal was secure and fit to continue once the route issue was cleared. I also asked the line staff to check whether the delay had created any further service impact on the return arrangement, and they confirmed the schedule change had been contained to the original movement.

After that, I updated the desk ledger, advised the traveler of the service status, and kept the matter open for follow-up. <<FACT F109>> I told the traveler that the desk would continue to monitor the booking until completion and would record any further issue without delay. The traveler remained cooperative throughout, and the animal was returned to standard care without further incident.

A follow-up review will be completed by the senior coordinator, with the welfare coordinator confirming that the handling record matches the final movement notes. The desk will also check whether any process step needs adjustment for future companion animal transfers. Companion Animal Travel Desk
